tracks.narration: What if a program could split itself in two — same code, same memory, but two living processes?
Here is a process P. It has its own code, its own heap, its own stack — a private little universe with one thread of control.
Then P calls fork. The kernel makes an exact copy of the address space. Now there are two processes — a parent and a child — each with the same memory and registers.
Both processes return from the very same call. The parent gets back the child's PID; the child gets back zero. That is how each one knows who it is.
One call. Two returns. Two processes — running concurrently from there.
